name: Erdős primes: primes p such that all p-k! for 1 <= k! < p are nonprime.
comment: Numbers of Erdős primes <= 10^j for j = 1,2,3, ... are 1, 1, 13, 95, 901, 7875, 71140, 646242, 5901409, ... For large j the asymptotic law seems to be #E(10^j) ~ (1/8)*(10^j/(j*log(10))). If so the sequence is infinite.
reference: Richard K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd Edition, Springer, 2004, Section A2, p. 11.
link: Amiram Eldar, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..10000 (terms 1..7875 from T. D. Noe)
mathematica: q[n_] := Module[{k = 1}, While[k! < n && ! PrimeQ[n - k!], k++]; k! >= n]; Select[Prime[Range[550]], q] (* _Amiram Eldar_, Mar 21 2024 *)
program: (PARI) isok(p) = { if(isprime(p), my(f=1,k=1); while (f < p && !isprime(p-f), k++; f*=k); f >= p, 0) } \\ _Harry J. Smith_, Sep 09 2009
